data.description:
## Description
**What**: Enumerate every forbidden-action HARD-GATE in the brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan SKILL.md files and encode each as a (skill, phase, forbidden-tool-or-action) tuple in a machine-readable registry that the PreToolUse hook consumes.
**Why**: The hook (draft-2) cannot decide whether to block a tool call without a data source mapping each phase to its forbidden tool/action set. This registry is the walking-skeleton data layer that the hook reads.
**Scope**:
- IN: Reading the four SKILL.md files, identifying each HARD-GATE forbidden-action statement, encoding it as a (skill, phase, forbidden-tool-or-action) tuple, writing the registry file, and a loader function that returns the forbidden set for a given (skill, phase).
- OUT: The hook that consumes the registry (draft-2); the override CLI (draft-3); any runtime tool interception.

## Done Definitions

- The registry file contains a (skill, phase, forbidden-tool-or-action) tuple for each forbidden-action HARD-GATE found in the brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan SKILL.md files ← Satisfies: sc-2
- A loader function returns the forbidden tool/action set for a given (skill, phase) pair and returns an empty set for a pair with no forbidden actions ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, including the loader function and registry parsing ← Satisfies: sc-2

## Considerations

- [Maintainability] The registry must stay in sync with the SKILL.md HARD-GATEs; encode the source skill and phase so drift is auditable.
- [Convention] Any new .sh file created for the loader sets the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation per project convention.
- [External-blocker] Phase-state shape is informed by sibling-epic infra (d076-d35e, 750c-6033) get_artifacts_dir() worktree resolution and session-state tracking; this story encodes the registry only and does not depend on an in-epic story for that infra.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a hook author, I want every forbidden-action HARD-GATE enumerated into a (skill, phase, forbidden-tool-or-action) registry, so the enforcement hook has a single data source to evaluate tool calls against
